properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05, closing the session and naming a tension he has been circling all day:

"The initial vision was, using a house as the delivered product, was that when you gave the house to somebody else, they would also get all the blueprints and design decisions (this would be the reflow2 graph). This would all come in a nice package that anybody else could take from there and see why you made the decisions you made and take it from there. In a code based project, your repo = implemented code + reflow graph object + other artifacts in a reflow blob storage. This would all come in one nice and complete package. However, in retrospec, this could have been done differently. The discussion earlier is more about collaboration and using multiple graphs, which somewhat break this wholistic/complete package that I had originally developed. Theoretically, there is no reason that you couldn't create a common/shared server that hosts the reflow2 mcp and everybody in the organization could access it. Not only that, a project could just point to the graph_id (or multiple graph_ids) and everybody could work collaboratively. Additionally, if people were assigned subsections of a big project, they could just point their .mcp.json at the master graph in their project and take on their subsection. So I guess what I'm stating is that to increase collaboration, we may have to remove the 'nicely wholistic combined package' that I had originally developed."

⭐ FIRST, MEASURED: BOTH HALVES ARE ALREADY ACCEPTED REQUIREMENTS, AND THE SHARED SERVER IS ALREADY BUILT.
  - `req:persistence` (ACCEPTED) — "The design persists in-repo alongside the code." The package.
  - `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo` (ACCEPTED) — "Someone without the repo can reach a design, read it, and contribute to it." The collaboration.
  - `req:content-reaches-every-seat` (ACCEPTED) — "a pointer resolves for everyone holding the design, not only for the seat that stored it."
  - `dec:central-host` — ACCEPTED (its NAME still reads "OPEN — does reflow2 gain a hosted surface…", which is stale in the same way `dec:skills-served`'s was; worth a rename, not a re-decision).
  - AND `--http` SHIPS TODAY: `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs` carries `--http`, `--http-allow-host` and `serve_http`, and its own comment says "`--http` already lets several sessions share one design, and it works."
So this is not a road not taken. The design committed to BOTH and the transport exists.

⭐⭐ SECOND, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: THE DICHOTOMY IS FALSE, BECAUSE THE PACKAGE AND THE WORKING MEDIUM WERE NEVER THE SAME ARTIFACT. The live store (`.reflow2/graph`) is GIT-IGNORED and always has been. What ships in the repo is `docs/design/reflow2.json` — the deterministic, self-contained, mergeable EXPORT. The house-with-blueprints has always been the export, never the store. So collaborating on a shared store does not touch the package: the package is what you export FROM it.

⚠️ THIRD, AND THIS IS WHERE HIS INSTINCT IS RIGHT AFTER ALL. The loss is real, and it is a DEFAULT rather than a capability:
  - With a per-repo store, the design is IN the repo by default and you must work to lose it.
  - With a shared server, the design is OUT of the repo by default and you must work to KEEP it.
That flip is the actual cost of collaboration, and it is not fixed by having an export format — it is fixed by something making the export happen. Which is why [BL-215] is the same finding from the other end: the hxm_program session found `.reflow2` git-ignored, and every captured decision had to be HAND-COPIED into markdown for teammates, "double bookkeeping, and only the prose copy is shared." That team already lost the package, on a per-repo store, with no shared server involved — because nothing told the project to commit its export.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) KEEP THE PER-REPO STORE AS THE DEFAULT and treat the shared server as the exception — today's shape. Counter: it is the shape that produced three stores on one repo and prose cross-references, and it makes the collaboration requirement something you configure your way into, which `reflow2_init.py`'s own comment already argues against for `--shared` ("a capability you have to reconfigure your way into is one most users never reach"). (b) SHARED SERVER AS THE DEFAULT, EXPORT AS THE DELIVERABLE — collaboration is normal, and committing the export becomes an explicit, prompted, possibly gated act. Counter: the export is only as fresh as the last person who ran it, so the package's completeness becomes a discipline rather than a property, and a stale export is a COMPLETE document that merges cleanly and silently drops work (`req:stale-seat-knows` names exactly this). (c) BOTH, WITH THE EXPORT AUTOMATED — a session-end hook or a CI job keeps the committed export fresh, so the package survives whichever medium the work happens in. Cheapest thing that preserves both accepted requirements, and it is [BL-215]'s own suggestion. Counter: nobody has said what happens when the automated export and a human's differ, and an export that writes itself is one more thing that can silently break. (d) THE PACKAGE IS THE POINT AND COLLABORATION SHOULD BEND TO IT — keep everything per-repo and solve sharing by merging exports, as `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (ACCEPTED) already says: "Many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service." Counter: that decision predates the field evidence, and one person on one machine already ended up with three stores and a markdown side-channel under it.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: `--http` exists and works; `req:persistence` and `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo` are BOTH accepted; the live store is git-ignored and the export is the shipped artifact; `dec:multi-writer-architecture` chose merge-on-pull over a hosted service and has not been revisited since the field reports; and `dec:central-host` is accepted despite a name that still says OPEN.

NOT CHECKED, and it bears on (b) and (c): whether a shared `--http` server can serve SEVERAL graph_ids at once, or is bound to one like the stdio server is. `dec:idea-many-graphs-one-store` measured that `with_graph_id` is free and the store namespaces by id, but nobody has looked at what the HTTP path does with that.
properties.name: OPEN — does collaborating on a shared server cost the self-contained package, or does it only flip which way the default points?
properties.rationale:
Captured at Anthony's request as the session's closing thought, and the mechanical half was checked first — which changed the answer twice. He believed he was describing a road not taken; both halves are accepted requirements and the transport ships. He believed collaboration would cost the package; the package is the export and was never the working store.

What survives his concern, and is recorded as the load-bearing sentence, is the DEFAULT flip: per-repo you must work to lose the design, shared you must work to keep it. That is a real cost, it is not an architectural one, and it is already being paid on a per-repo store by the team in [BL-215] — which is the strongest evidence that the threat was never the shared server.

Deliberately not registered as alternatives, so the loop does not start asking him to choose. He asked for this to be the last activity of the session and to keep nothing promoted; four options with their counters is the state he asked for.
